newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli soldier, guerrilla killed in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldier, guerrilla killed in Lebanon.

text.p: One Israeli soldier was killed and two others were wounded on Friday when Hizbollah guerrillas shelled their post in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, pro-Israeli militia sources said.
The pro-Iranian group, which claimed responsbility for the attack, said one of its fighters was killed in the ensuing clashes with the Israeli forces in the early morning.

The guerrillas fired mortar bombs at Dabsheh and Ali Taher posts on the edge of the Israeli-held zone, the South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia sources said. One Israeli soldier was killed and two wounded as a result of the bombardment on Dabsheh, they added.
There was no immediate confirmation of the casualties from the Israeli army.

Hours after the attack, Israeli warplanes raided suspected guerrilla targets north of the zone, security sources said. Two jets fired two rockets into the Habboush river area just north of the south Lebanon zone.
SLA sources confirmed the air attack. There was no immediate word on casualties in the air raid, the 19th into Lebanon this year.
Friday's Israeli fatality raised to five the number of Israeli soldiers killed in south Lebanon this year. Last year, 27 Israeli soldiers died in Lebanon fighting.
In Beirut, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah claimed responsibility for the assaults on Dabsheh and Ali Taher.
SLA sources also said two guerrillas were killed on Thursday night when Israeli helicopters and artillery gunners fired at a group of fighters trying to infiltrate the zone.
It was not immediately clear to which group the slain guerrillas belonged. There was no confirmation of the report from security sources or Hizbollah.
Hizbollah (Party of God) is fighting to oust some 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 SLA militiamen from the south Lebanon zone set up to prevent guerrilla attacks on northern Israel.
